items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I can remember one lady dancing, her name was Catherine, they called her Blondie. She was the wife, now, of Count Basie.

ctx.x: We worked hard, and rehearsed every week to try to improve the band and keep the patrons coming. We used the same style of cabaret as we did at Mammy Louise's Creole Garden. We had a singer named Rutherford, he had a rich, golden voice, baritone voice, and he could sing "Old Man River" and make you cry.

We had several great singers, that worked at this particular club. And I can remember one lady dancing, her name was Catherine, they called her Blondie. She was the wife, now, of Count Basie. We had a beautiful relationship with the owner of the club, and with all the employees there, during our tenure at the Furnace Nightclub.

We also did some charitable work. Playing at the Phyllis Wheatly Club, and the Delta Sorority, on their Founder's day. And several times we were called onto give our services free of charge, which we did. We saved our money and saved enough money to buy brand new uniforms. Back in those days they were wearing the bi-swing suit. And we had suits made and the band made a beautiful appearance.
